blocks.text: Bar charts are ideal for comparing different categories. Each bar represents a category, and the height (or length) of the bar indicates the value associated with that category.
Example: Imagine you want to compare the sales figures for different products in a store. A bar chart can visually represent this data.

blocks.alt: Grouped bar chart titled Sales on Day 1 and Day 2 for various items. The vertical axis, Number of products sold, runs to 1000. Four pairs of bars (Day 1 blue, Day 2 yellow): 800 and 600; 800 and 1000; 1000 and 600; 400 and 600.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.4: A bar chart showing sales figures of different products (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.4).
